access.name: Invoice ownership
access.title: Review: Invoice ownership
access.intro: A pull request is a proposed code change. Compare this example, understand the risk, then inspect the fix.
access.impact: A changed invoice ID could expose another customer’s bill.
access.fix: Check ownership on the server before returning an invoice. The current user must come from a trusted authenticated session.
access.instruction: Check ownership on the server before returning an invoice. The current user must come from a trusted authenticated session.
access.limit: Try owner, different user, anonymous user and missing invoice against every read/update route. Verify tenant isolation and server-side identity.

config.name: Debug responses
config.title: Review: Debug responses
config.intro: A pull request is a proposed code change. Compare this example, understand the risk, then inspect the fix.
config.impact: Debug mode can expose detailed exception traces to visitors.
config.fix: Disable debug responses and keep diagnostics in protected server logs.
config.instruction: Disable debug responses and keep diagnostics in protected server logs.
config.limit: The rule matches literal FastAPI(debug=True) only. Inspect deployed settings and trigger a controlled exception to confirm no diagnostic data leaks.

supply.name: Dependency release gates
supply.title: Review: Dependency release gates
supply.intro: A pull request is a proposed code change. Compare this example, understand the risk, then inspect the fix.
supply.impact: Untracked, unaudited dependencies can introduce vulnerable or compromised code into a release.
supply.fix: Use a reviewed hash-locked dependency set, provenance checks, current audits and an inventory. The fixed fixture describes required pipeline gates, not an implemented build system.
supply.instruction: Use a reviewed hash-locked dependency set, provenance checks, current audits and an inventory. The fixed fixture describes required pipeline gates, not an implemented build system.
supply.limit: Verify the actual lock, hashes, provenance identities, transitive audit, SBOM and update process. Fail each gate deliberately; hashing alone does not prove a dependency safe.

tls.name: TLS certificate verification
tls.title: Review: TLS certificate verification
tls.intro: A pull request is a proposed code change. Compare this example, understand the risk, then inspect the fix.
tls.impact: verify=False disables certificate-chain and hostname checks. An intercepting attacker could impersonate the HTTPS server even though traffic is encrypted.
tls.fix: Use the Requests default certificate verification or explicit verify=True. Keep a timeout; it does not replace identity validation.
tls.instruction: Use the Requests default certificate verification or explicit verify=True. Keep a timeout; it does not replace identity validation.
tls.limit: The rule checks literal verify=False in requests.get/post/request only. Validate the actual trust store and certificate failure behavior separately; no network request runs here.

sql.name: SQL parameter binding
sql.title: Review: SQL parameter binding
sql.intro: A pull request is a proposed code change. Compare this example, understand the risk, then inspect the fix.
sql.impact: A customer name concatenated into SQL can change the database instruction.
sql.fix: Use a query placeholder with a separately bound value so input stays data.
sql.instruction: Use a query placeholder with a separately bound value so input stays data.
sql.limit: This rule targets concatenation directly inside execute. It does not cover every query builder, dynamic identifier or injection path.

design.name: One coupon per customer
design.title: Review: One coupon per customer
design.intro: A pull request is a proposed code change. Compare this example, understand the risk, then inspect the fix.
design.impact: Without a redemption limit, a customer can repeatedly claim the same credit, including through concurrent requests.
design.fix: Define a one-redemption invariant and enforce it atomically with credit issuance. The fixed fixture illustrates a transaction and uniqueness contract.
design.finding: One coupon per customer needs attention
design.instruction: Define a one-redemption invariant and enforce it atomically with credit issuance. The fixed fixture illustrates a transaction and uniqueness contract.
design.limit: Threat-model abuse and test concurrent/replayed requests, rollback and cross-account rules against the real database. A method name cannot establish atomicity.

auth.name: Session rotation at login
auth.title: Review: Session rotation at login
auth.intro: A pull request is a proposed code change. Compare this example, understand the risk, then inspect the fix.
auth.impact: Reusing the pre-login session identifier can let someone who knows that identifier inherit the authenticated session.
auth.fix: Rotate the session identifier after verified login and invalidate the previous identifier atomically. The session service must implement this contract.
auth.finding: Session rotation at login needs attention
auth.instruction: Rotate the session identifier after verified login and invalidate the previous identifier atomically. The session service must implement this contract.
auth.limit: Confirm old sessions fail, new identifiers are unpredictable, cookies are Secure/HttpOnly with appropriate SameSite, and expiry/logout work. Also assess MFA and login abuse controls.

yaml.name: Safe YAML deserialization
yaml.category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures
yaml.title: Review: Safe YAML deserialization
yaml.intro: A pull request is a proposed code change. Compare this example, understand the risk, then inspect the fix.
yaml.impact: An unsafe YAML loader can construct Python objects from untrusted tagged data.
yaml.fix: Use safe_load, bound input size, and validate expected keys, types and ranges.
yaml.instruction: Use safe_load, bound input size, and validate expected keys, types and ranges.
yaml.limit: This rule detects selected unsafe YAML loaders only. safe_load does not authenticate the sender, prove data integrity or eliminate all resource risks.

logging.name: Observable access denials
logging.category: A09:2025 Security Logging and Alerting Failures
logging.title: Review: Observable access denials
logging.intro: A pull request is a proposed code change. Compare this example, understand the risk, then inspect the fix.
logging.impact: Unrecorded access denials can hide repeated attempts to reach protected records.
logging.fix: Record structured security events without credentials, protect storage, and configure actionable alert routing with an accountable responder.
logging.instruction: Record structured security events without credentials, protect storage, and configure actionable alert routing with an accountable responder.
logging.limit: The lab records synthetic events and a threshold alert in memory, sending nothing externally. Real protected retention, redaction, alert delivery and human response still need integration tests.

errors.name: Fail closed on timeout
errors.title: Review: Fail closed on timeout
errors.intro: A pull request is a proposed code change. Compare this example, understand the risk, then inspect the fix.
errors.impact: Granting access when a policy service times out turns an outage into an authorization bypass.
errors.fix: Deny access on the illustrated timeout. The caller should expose a safe error and record the outage.
errors.finding: Fail closed on timeout needs attention
errors.instruction: Deny access on the illustrated timeout. The caller should expose a safe error and record the outage.
errors.limit: The lab checks a healthy allow and denial on timeout. Real-service failures, cleanup, rollback, safe responses and bounded retries need separate validation.
